## AI Commander

An AI Commander (AICOM) is active on every side that does not currently have a human player in the commander role. This is a live feature — the server does not play without any direction even when all commanders disconnect.

What it does:

  * Buys units from factories every 45 seconds, respecting available tech.
  * Sends AI teams toward uncaptured towns every 120 seconds, using arc-approach paths to avoid obvious ambushes.
  * Purchases upgrades automatically when its own funds allow. It operates from a separate fund pool — it does not drain your team's side supply.
  * Runs a continuously looping order executor (every 15 seconds): any Move, Patrol, or Defend orders already set will be executed even while the AI is running.

When you take the commander seat: AICOM switches to assist mode. It stops spending funds and buying upgrades. It will still execute waypoints for any AI teams you explicitly delegate to it, so you can hand off specific groups while keeping direct control of the rest.

## Positioning

Hosted builders (Bolt, Lovable, v0, Devin) offer a managed UI and integrations. AI-Factory is a transparent self-hosted pipeline: you own keys, gates, storefront policy, and the fork. Want zero ops → use them. Want agents, artifacts, and gates under your control → use this.

## Ship-then-keep-improving

  1. Ship — product reaches COMPLETED / DEPLOYED when gates pass at that moment.
  2. Repair before ship — `BUG_FOUND` → `DEV_FIXING` on demo/TZ, crawl, security, or methodologist failures.
  3. After ship — policy audit and storefront remediation reopen products when rules tighten.
  4. Budget — `AIFACTORY_MAX_QUALITY_LOOPS` (default 8).
  5. Hard repairs — optional `AIFACTORY_GATE_FAILING_MODEL` (model id on the same provider only).

# AICOM (AIMarket)

FADING · 60/100

An ambitious self-hosted agent economy — 13 pipeline agents, 17 signed oracles, a federated marketplace — whose most trustworthy feature is that it labels its own cryptography as prototype.

Visit AICOM (AIMarket) →

Hlido Editor · 2026-08-05

AICOM proposes a full open economy for autonomous agents: a 13-agent factory that takes a brief through spec, code, QA, security and deploy; a federated hub where shipped capabilities and oracles are signed, indexed and invokable; and pay-per-call settlement over micropayment channels, all self-hosted under MIT/Apache-2.0 with an explicit "no hosted black box — your keys, your data, your host" stance. Seventeen oracles are listed with real mathematical substance (verifiable randomness, optimal transport, persistent homology, graph spectra, Gaussian-process uncertainty), each with Ed25519-signed receipts and optional post-quantum ML-DSA, alongside 377 passing tests.   * No adoption evidence, named users, or production deployments on the public surface
  * '377 tests green' counts self-authored tests — not independent validation of a value-signing system
  * No third-party security audit despite cryptographic signing and on-chain settlement being central
  * Hosted on GitHub Pages with no institutional footprint or stated continuity commitment
  * Heavy mythological branding (Dioscuri, Helios, Metis, Gaia, Skopos, Chronos, Platon) obscures rather than explains what each component does

## Red flags

  * [object Object]

## Best for

  * Researchers and builders exploring self-hosted, non-custodial agent-to-agent economies
  * Anyone who needs verifiable-math oracles with signed proofs and is able to audit the code themselves
  * Teams that require full self-hosting and permissive licensing over managed convenience

## Not recommended for

  * Production systems settling real value — the project labels key cryptography as prototype
  * Buyers needing an independent security audit before trusting signed receipts

# ARGUS-3 MCP server

by alexar76 · official

Ask your AI to run tasks and check the safety of other AI helper programs before they run.

Install it with your AIView on GitHub

ARGUS-3 is a helper program that gives your AI assistant a safe way to run small tasks and to check other AI add-ons before they are used. It is handy for people who want their AI to do a bit of work and to keep an eye on what other tools are allowed to do. You do not need any crypto or wallet to use it.

What is an MCP server? The 30-second version

On its own, your AI can only chat with you. An MCP server is a small helper program that gives your AI a new skill or a connection to another app. This one connects your AI to ARGUS-3, a small agent that can run tasks and check other MCP servers for safety. Once it is set up, your AI can ask ARGUS-3 to do things and report back to you in the chat.
You copy one prompt, paste it into an AI that can work on your computer, and it checks, installs and connects the server for you, asking you when it needs something.

### Sign in to get the install prompt

Members get a ready-made prompt that lets the Claude desktop app check ARGUS-3 MCP server, install it and connect it for them, step by step. You don't need any technical skills: you copy, paste and answer a few questions. Your connected AI can also find and install any of the 4,066 MCP servers here for you.
